newsitem.title: JAPAN: EPA view of Japan economy stronger.
newsitem.headline: EPA view of Japan economy stronger.

text.p: The Japanese Economic Planning Agency's assessment of Japan's economy is "half-a-step" or "two-thirds-of-a-step" stronger than it was a month ago, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Friday morning.
Aso also quoted Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita as telling this morning's cabinet meeting that Japan's economy is continuing its gradual recovery.
Matsushita was also quoted as saying that the BOJ's assessment of the economy was almost in line with the results of the BOJ's June "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment.
Aso said that the negative impact of an increase in Japan's consumption tax on April 1 was almost complete in June.
"The economy is firming up," Aso said.

Asked if a stronger assessment of the economy would allow the BOJ to stop keeping short-term interest rates at current low levels, Aso said, "Economic conditions in and after July must be carefully monitored before such a question is considered."
